Research question is answered and ready to drive execution.

Each finding is annotated with the file:line reference supporting (or adjusting) it. Critical Finding 6 (webhook atomicity gap) is directly reproducible at stripe_webhook_service.go:191-195 (status update via s.db.Exec) followed by :226 call to handleSubscriptionCompletion which opens its own connection at :245 — no shared transaction.

evidence.title: Finding 6 atomicity gap — source excerpt
evidence.description: The highest-risk finding is exactly as described. In stripe_webhook_service.go:handleCheckoutCompleted, the checkout_sessions.status update (lines 191-195) uses s.db.Exec directly (no transaction), and the subsequent call to handleSubscriptionCompletion (line 226) executes INSERT INTO subscriptions ... ON CONFLICT DO UPDATE (line 245-249) on a separate connection. A failure after the status update commits leaves checkout_sessions marked 'complete' with no subscription row. This is the silent partial-failure mode Action 1 addresses.

test_results.name: checkout_sessions status update is outside a transaction
test_results.output_summary: stripe_webhook_service.go:191-195 uses s.db.Exec() directly; no BEGIN/COMMIT wrapper.

test_results.name: subscription insert runs in a different execution context
test_results.output_summary: stripe_webhook_service.go:226 calls handleSubscriptionCompletion which runs its own INSERT/ON CONFLICT at :245-249; no shared tx handle.

test_results.name: Silent partial-failure scenario is reachable
test_results.output_summary: If the second call errors, status='complete' is already committed. No detection mechanism exists in-tree; intro_anomaly_log does not cover this case.

improvement_suggestions.description: Correct spec.json status from 'failed' to 'completed' (or 'archived') before archival — conclusion.md is substantive and the deliverable is complete. Status='failed' will misclassify this item in overview/stats dashboards.

Research conclusions that reference specific symbol names and line numbers should be validated by a lint step (or a pre-archive hook) that resolves each file:line/symbol reference against the repo. This would have caught the insertOrUpdateSubscription naming drift and the line-number off-by-ones automatically rather than relying on manual review.

Action 1's execute item should include a regression test that simulates subscription-insert failure after the checkout_sessions status update and asserts the status update is rolled back (transactional atomicity). Without this test, future refactors could silently reintroduce the gap.
